div.span: Click an ecosystem above to narrow everything below it.

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_hostecostate_lookup | where hostname="__fleet__" | search $eco_filter$ | rename instances AS components | stats sum(components) AS components, sum(with_identifier) AS with_identifier BY type | eval without_identifier = components - with_identifier | eval identifier_pct = round(with_identifier * 100 / components, 1) | sort 50000 - components | rename type AS "Ecosystem", components AS "Components", with_identifier AS "With purl/cpe", without_identifier AS "No identifier", identifier_pct AS "Identifiable %"

| `riskability_open_findings` | search ecosystem=$eco_name|s$ | eval root = if(scope_id!="", scope_id, "host") | stats dc(package) AS packages, dc(cve_id) AS cves BY root, hostname | sort 50000 - packages | rename root AS "Root", hostname AS "Host", packages AS "Packages", cves AS "CVEs"

| inputlookup riskability_hostecostate_lookup | where hostname="__fleet__" | search $eco_filter$ | stats sum(instances) AS components, sum(cpe_ident) AS cpe_ident BY type | append [| `riskability_feed_ecosystems` | rename ecosystem AS type] | eventstats max(eval(if(type=="cpe", feed_ranges, null()))) AS cpe_ranges | stats max(components) AS components, max(cpe_ident) AS cpe_ident, max(feed_packages) AS feed_packages, max(feed_ranges) AS feed_ranges, max(cpe_ranges) AS cpe_ranges BY type | where isnotnull(components) | eval feed_packages = coalesce(feed_packages, 0), feed_ranges = coalesce(feed_ranges, 0) | eval status = case( feed_ranges > 0, "covered", cpe_ident > 0 AND cpe_ranges > 0, "covered through CPE", type IN ("linux-kernel-module","linux-kernel","github-action","github-action-workflow","binary","hotfix"), "no feed exists for this type", 1=1, "add this ecosystem to the bundle") | eval reach = case(feed_ranges > 0, tostring(feed_ranges, "commas"), cpe_ident > 0 AND cpe_ranges > 0, tostring(cpe_ranges, "commas") . " CPE ranges", 1=1, "0") | eval feed_packages = if(feed_packages < 0, "counted approximately", tostring(feed_packages, "commas")) | sort 50000 - components | rename type AS "Ecosystem", components AS "Components in fleet", feed_packages AS "Packages in feed", reach AS "Version ranges reachable", status AS "Status" | fields "Ecosystem", "Components in fleet", "Packages in feed", "Version ranges reachable", "Status"

viz.option: Every ecosystem in the fleet is covered by the imported feed - the one empty table here that is good news.

panel.title: Did everything the collector found actually arrive?

search.query: sourcetype=riskability:swinv index=`riskability_index_inventory` NOT record_type=* | eventstats max(_time) AS rk_newest BY hostname | where _time >= rk_newest | stats count AS arrived BY hostname | append [| inputlookup riskability_links_hoststate_lookup | table hostname, link_rows] | stats sum(arrived) AS arrived, sum(link_rows) AS links_arrived BY hostname | lookup riskability_scanstate_lookup hostname OUTPUT said_components, said_link, sources_failed, failed_text, swinv_version, scanned_at | eval arrived = coalesce(arrived, 0), links_arrived = coalesce(links_arrived, 0) | eval shortfall = if(isnull(said_components), null(), said_components - arrived) | eval pct = if(isnull(said_components) OR said_components = 0, null(), round(arrived * 100 / said_components, 1)) | eval verdict = case( isnull(said_components), "collector does not report a manifest", sources_failed > 0, "a source failed on the host", shortfall > 0, "components went missing on the way in", 1=1, "everything arrived") | eval reported = strftime(scanned_at, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M") | sort 5000 - shortfall | table hostname, verdict, swinv_version, said_components, arrived, pct, said_link, links_arrived, failed_text, reported | rename hostname AS "Host", verdict AS "Verdict", swinv_version AS "Collector", said_components AS "Collector found", arrived AS "Reached the index", pct AS "Arrived %", said_link AS "Links found", links_arrived AS "Links stored", failed_text AS "Sources that failed", reported AS "Scanned at"

div.b: This is the only panel that can catch data lost on the way in.
div.span: swinv states in every scan how many components it found. Everything downstream reports success whether or not those components arrive, so without comparing the two, a host that collected 3,993 components and delivered 15 looks exactly like a small host with nothing wrong. It then produces no findings, correctly, and the fleet reads as clean. A shortfall here almost always means index-time parsing: check that the swinv sourcetype's line breaking is present on the indexers, not only on the search heads. "A source failed on the host" is the other direction: the collector could not read a package database, which is not the same as the host having no packages, and only the collector can tell you which.
